messages:
mika (support): FYI customer reported invalid JSON when using json_mode=structured + streaming. They sent a repro and we can reproduce with small prompt.

ingrid (eng): Can you paste the raw stream chunks? streaming often splits escapes across boundaries.

mika (support): Here's a minimal repro payload we used:
```
POST /v1/generate
Authorization: Bearer <key>
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "model": "rwd-3b",
  "json_mode": true,
  "stream": true,
  "input": "Please emit a JSON object with a path field and a note field. The path should be a Windows path: C:\\Users\\Alice\\notes.txt and the note should include a quote: \"She said: \\\"hello\\\"\""
}
```

mika (support): Stream we got (chunks concatenated):
```
{
  "path": "C:\Users\Alice\notes.txt",
  "note": "She said: \"hello\""
}
...then the stream cut and next chunk started with:

\"extra\": "trailing"}
```

ingrid (eng): Looks like a chunk boundary split a quoted string. The client reconnected and emitted the next chunk starting with an extra quote, producing an unbalanced string.

alex (runtime): Two issues: 1) streaming currently doesn't guarantee split-safe escape tokens; backslash sequences (\\uXXXX or \\) can be cut mid-sequence. 2) if client retries without de-dup, we can end up with duplicate/trailing fragments.

mika (support): Customer also saw a billing spike because their client retried the request 3x before giving up. They reported ~3x token usage.

samuel (billing): Can you send me the request IDs? we'll flag the invoice for review if this is a retry storm caused by broken clients.

mika (support): Request IDs: req_01F7... and req_01F8... (from the ticket).

ingrid (eng): Repro steps I used locally: run the curl above against staging with stream=1 and kill the TCP connection mid-response (SIGINT) then immediately re-open with same key and replay. I can reproduce unclosed-string parse error in consumer JSON parser.

alex (runtime): Short-term mitigation: suggest client to buffer stream until a terminating newline or explicit end-of-message marker, or use non-streaming mode for structured JSON. We should also recommend exponential backoff + idempotency key so retries don't double-bill.

mika (support): I'll send these mitigations to the customer. Also flagged docs to call out Windows paths as common footgun.

ingrid (eng): Longer term: runtime should try to align chunk boundaries on safe escape boundaries when json_mode=true. We can detect if last chunk ends in an odd number of backslashes or inside an open UTF-8 escape and delay sending until safe. Low-risk heuristic: if chunk ends with an unescaped backslash or an odd number of trailing backslashes, hold until next fragment aggregated.

alex (runtime): Agreed. Also add server-side idempotency header handling that ignores duplicate streaming sessions with same id within short window to avoid double-counting. That will help billing.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: runtime/streaming-chunk-fix (staging) -> 1718505000

mika (support): Customer asked for an immediate workaround in their node client. Suggested patch: replace backslashes in path fields before sending, e.g., path.replace(/\\/g, '\\\\') or base64-encode fields that may contain raw backslashes/quotes. They replied they'll try base64 for now. :thumbsup:

samuel (billing): I've placed a provisional credit on the account while eng investigates. Please keep ticket updated with repro and final fix plan.

ingrid (eng): I'll open a small RFC for runtime change and include tests for escape-safe chunking + a streaming-integration test that kills connections mid-string.

mika (support): Thanks team. I'll post a short KB entry and link to the ticket. If anyone wants the raw tcpdump from my repro, DM me.

alex (runtime): One more note: UTF-8 surrogate pairs can also be split (emoji). When that happens downstream JSON parsers choke. We should include tests for surrogate splits as well.

mika (support): Noted. Closing slack thread but keeping ticket open until staging fix lands.
